Subject: Expanding to 3 more clinical teams — timeline & keys

Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a quick internal sync and the directors for Virtual Intake, Prior Auth, and Patient Outreach want to move forward with pilot projects next quarter. High level ask: 3 new isolated API key namespaces (one per team), capacity for a combined 120qps burst, and a coordinated 6-week canary rollout.

Questions we have today:
- Can you provision isolated keys scoped per team with usage visibility for each namespace?
- What does a 6-week canary plan look like operationally (stages, rollback triggers)?
- Any contract/term change required to support the higher burst capacity and extra keys?

I attached a short summary of the projects (Aurora_Rollout_SOW_v2.pdf) — happy to set a call this week.

Best,
Claire Jensen
Director, AI Platforms
Aurora Health

Hi Claire — thanks for the note and the SOW, looks clear. Short answers up front:
- Yes, we can create three isolated API key namespaces with per-namespace usage dashboards and token-level billing.
- We typically run a staged canary over 4–6 weeks: internal smoke → pilot with 1 clinic → gradual ramp to full team traffic, with automatic fallback to the existing model variant if latency/regression thresholds are hit.
- For the burst profile and extra keys we can do a term amendment (one-page) to bump committed capacity and add a temporary burst pool; we can also add an option for annual committed capacity if you want pricing certainty.

Next steps I propose: 1) quick triage call today or tomorrow to confirm SSO/KMS needs; 2) I’ll draft an amendment and a simplified mutual action plan (MAP) that shows milestones and owners.

Available: Thu 3–5pm PT or Fri 8–11am PT. What works?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

Karthik / Aditya —
Couple of ops items to flag for the MAP and SOW update:
- Keys: we'll issue three namespaces (aurora-vi, aurora-pa, aurora-po). Each will have independent quotas and can be mapped to different rate classes.
- Burst: to hit 120 qps safely we recommend reserving a small Dedicated pool for the peak hours and rely on smart routing for off-peak. Cost estimate attached in the runbook.
- Security: Claire please confirm if keys need to be tenant-scoped + KMS-managed or if standard Redwood-managed keys are acceptable. We can support both, but KMS adds a couple of days to provisioning.

I attached a short canary checklist (Canary_Runbook.md) — I'll incorporate the dates once Karthik confirms the kickoff.

Claire / Procurement team —
Attached is the one-page amendment draft plus a short MAP outlining owners, milestones, and rollback criteria. Key commercial points:
- Term: 12 months amendment that adds 3 per-namespace API keys and increases burst capacity with a 30% committed uplift (option to convert to annual commit at renewal).
- Pricing: additional committed block priced at $X/month; on-demand burst priced per token above committed usage.
- SLA: 99.9% for latency, with automatic failover to lower-cost variant in case of capacity constraints.

Operational MAP highlights:
1) Week 0 — Provision KMS integration + issue namespaces (Marissa)
2) Week 1–2 — Internal smoke + pilot with Virtual Intake (Mateo)
3) Week 3–4 — Gradual ramp to Prior Auth and Patient Outreach
4) Week 5–6 — Full traffic shift and monitoring window; rollback if model regression >1.5% on key evals or 95th latency breach >400ms

I'll queue the DocuSign link for signatures once we have procurement confirmation on pricing. HubSpot deal linked here: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345678

Thanks,
Karthik
